sources.title: NOAA-20 Sees Low-Pressure System Spinning Off the Coast of South America
notes: Low-pressure systems rotate counterclockwise in the Northern Hemisphere and clockwise in the Southern Hemisphere because of the Coriolis effect.
Converging air is deflected to one side as it moves toward the centre.

sources.title: The Coriolis Effect
notes: Air rushing toward the low-pressure eye is deflected, so the whole system spins.
The equator moves faster than the poles because Earth is widest in the middle.
